THE ROWS WERE NOT DROPPED - every one of them exists in cases.json today under its new number, and CASE-0151 is CASE-0184. The whole block of eleven is declared, not only the one id a gate happens to have flagged, because all eleven were retired by the same commit for the same reason and declaring one would record a narrower fact than the true one.

Retired on 2026-09-03 by re-running planning/test-campaign/bin/win-cases-from-lane.py, which writes a `manual:<surface>` case only for a surface whose registry status is `manual`. SURF-044 - the Windows Discover detail dialog - reads `status: ready` in surfaces-windows.json and did so at the baseline commit too, so this row had been stale since the status changed and nobody re-ran the generator. Its whole content was the sentence 'not reachable from the shell's navigation, so the destination sweep never opens it', which is no longer true: shell-lane.ps1 section 3b opens that dialog through the automation plane from a real store row (the discover.detail arm). NOT A LOSS OF COVERAGE - SURF-044 keeps CASE-0347, CASE-0349, CASE-0404 and CASE-0405, and gains the generated discover.detail row; what left was an `n/a:` placeholder claiming the surface was unreachable. Four reckoning records cite the number (planning/reckoning/2026-09-02, 2026-09-02T2200, 2026-09-03 and planning/evidence/wa4-reckoning-after) and those citations were correct on the day they were written, which is why this is declared here rather than by editing them.
